response.goal: Fix the n8n workflow so the full CSV file of about 5,000 rows lands in Google Sheets every night, with retries and a Slack message if it still fails.

plan.step: Analyze the current n8n workflow and diagnose the Google Sheets 429 Too Many Requests error during batch appends.
Modify the workflow to batch rows properly and add rate-limiting or retry logic to handle API limits.
Integrate a Slack notification node to alert the team if the workflow fails after retries.
Test the updated workflow with the full 5,000-row file and verify successful delivery.

milestones.name: Diagnosis and Workflow Refactoring
milestones.deliverable: Updated n8n workflow with batching, rate-limiting, and retry logic.

milestones.name: Testing and Slack Alert Integration
milestones.deliverable: Fully tested import of the 5,000-row file and active Slack failure alerts.

proof_map.step: Analyze the current n8n workflow and diagnose the Google Sheets 429 Too Many Requests error during batch appends.

risks.risk: Google Sheets API rate limits (429) may persist if batch sizes or append frequencies are still too high.
risks.mitigation: Implement explicit chunking (e.g., splitting into smaller batches with short pauses) within the n8n workflow.

questions: What specific Google Sheets node configuration or batch size is currently being used?
Which Slack channel should the failure alert messages be sent to?
assumptions: The fixed budget of $250 matches the scope of fixing and testing the nightly import workflow.
Access to the existing n8n instance and Google/Slack accounts will be provided.
